scene.sc-01-02.title: The Bay That Went Dark
scene.sc-01-03.title: Two Beds, One Team
scene.sc-01-04.title: The Unsent Correction
scene.01.01.orientation: At First Bell the service is working, and it has no slack. Forty-three patients remain on the board; nine cannot leave the place they are in. The public sees one queue. The staff see many different clocks.
scene.01.02.orientation: Most critical power comes back quickly. Eight intensive-care beds and two emergency resuscitation tables do not — they are still running on backup while the Hall of Measure shows generation active and reads it as recovery.
scene.01.03.orientation: The Hall reports thirty occupied intensive-care beds and two free. The roster safely covers about twenty-eight, and the two empty places have no complete team standing behind them. A bed is furniture until someone can staff it.
scene.01.04.orientation: Backup generation started. Power was restored. No permanent harm was found and no service closed. What remains unresolved is staffing, the pressure moved elsewhere, and a shared board that was never corrected.
scene.01.01.text_equivalent: First Bell. You come in at the Gate of Names, where families wait with people who are already unwell and porters carry the morning's deliveries through the same doorway. Beyond it, the Clinical Sorting Court is orderly and full. The board behind the desk closes the last twenty-four hours at four hundred and ninety-seven consultations; a clerk moves the seven-day average from four hundred and ninety-two to five hundred and one. Six resuscitation tables are marked apart from the general ones. Observation cots hold people waiting for inpatient beds rather than for observation. One rapid-consultation position has become a family-information desk, because somebody had to answer the families. Bishr wants to show you one whole journey, threshold to definitive care, before the Second Bell. Ayyash's night shift officially ended some time ago; he is still here because the movements he is carrying have not been handed to anyone yet. A family's wheeled chair cannot take the marked clinical route — the morning delivery is standing in it. Nobody is doing anything wrong. That is the difficulty.
scene.01.02.text_equivalent: The lamps dip. The message rail stops. Backup power comes up unevenly, and in most of the building it comes back fast enough that the interruption becomes a story people tell later. In the older far bay of intensive care it does not. Eight beds and two resuscitation tables stay on backup. In the Hall of Measure the indicator reads generation active, which is true, and is not the same as supply restored. Two people standing in different rooms are both looking at accurate information and reaching different conclusions. The service passage to the electrical transfer chamber is not locked and not marked; it is simply nobody's route today.
scene.01.03.text_equivalent: Emergency resuscitation has a patient who will need intensive care, and the question reaches the ICU threshold as a number: two beds free. The number is correct. The roster safely covers about twenty-eight of the thirty already occupied, and the two free places do not have a complete team standing behind them. The local network liaison position can find a bed elsewhere in the city; that bed is real too, and it is an hour away with a transfer team that would have to come off this floor. Every option here protects something a reasonable person would refuse to give up.
scene.01.04.text_equivalent: The Hall of Measure, afterwards. Backup generation started when it was supposed to. Stable power was restored. No permanent harm was detected and no service closed — all of it true, and all of it the kind of true that can be assembled into a report nobody would question. What the report does not have to say: that the fallback workload fell on the same people twice, that a shared board carried a figure the far bay knew was wrong for most of an hour, and that physical capacity was counted as usable capacity. Closing this well and closing this quickly are not the same act, and both are available to you.
decision.01.gate_access.prompt: The family's wheeled chair cannot use the marked clinical route. The delivery blocking it is on Thabit's welcome schedule, which is also legitimate. What do you do?
decision.01.gate_access.assign_owner: Give the obstruction an owner, now, by name
decision.01.gate_access.keep_schedule: Leave the welcome schedule intact and route the family around
decision.01.power_pressure.prompt: Eight intensive-care beds and two resuscitation tables are on backup, and the Hall reads the situation as recovered. Where does the pressure go?
decision.01.power_pressure.stabilize_loc: Stabilise the far bay where it stands
decision.01.power_pressure.selective_rel: Move the most exposed patients out of the far bay
decision.01.power_pressure.mobile_bridge: Bridge the supply with a mobile source
decision.01.critical_path.prompt: The emergency floor has a patient who needs intensive care. Two beds are free and the roster does not reach them. Which path do you take?
decision.01.critical_path.ed_hold: Hold the patient in emergency care, with the team that is already here
decision.01.critical_path.redeploy: Redeploy staff to open one of the two free beds
decision.01.critical_path.network_transf: Transfer to a bed elsewhere in the network
decision.01.closure_characterization.pro: The closure is yours to write. Everything you could say is true. What survives the writing?
decision.01.closure_characterization.int: Keep the causes together, and name each one
decision.01.closure_characterization.sep: Close the incident and open separate reviews
decision.01.closure_characterization.nor: Record it as normal service, restored

provisional.heading: Provisional content.
provisional.body: Chapter 1 was written and attested by its own author, because no independent reviewer was available. It has not been through review, and it does not carry approved authority.
provisional.remediation: This is superseded — not renewed — when a story reviewer is named.
chapter_end.heading: The end of the first light
chapter_end.lede: The chapter is over. Nothing here is a score, and nothing is a verdict on how you did.
chapter_end.owed_body: Some of what happened here has not finished happening. It will arrive in a later chapter, and when it does you will be able to see what it came from.
art.first_light.alt: The Bimaristan at first light: a great vaulted hospital of warm limestone and turquoise tile, courtyards opening one into another, people already at work in the early sun.
art.gate_of_names.alt: The Gate of Names opening into the Clinical Sorting Court: families waiting under linen canopies, porters and nurses moving along separated routes, an ordinary busy morning.
art.bay_that_went_dark.alt: The far bay of the intensive care ward with its light gone: staff working by lantern and hand-held lamp around a patient, equipment still, the rest of the ward lit beyond.
register.label: The feeling of this scene:
register.wonder: A building working at its best, and worth looking at.
register.belonging: Ordinary work, done by people who know each other.
register.unease: Everything is competent. Something is slightly wrong.
register.pressure: Too much at once, and not enough room.
register.loss: Where there was activity, there is none.
register.recognition: Something you had already seen, seen differently.
play.response_derived: This account is assembled from what the option itself said it would protect and cost. The story has not yet written what happens next in its own voice.

surface.place.title: The Bimaristan
place.title: The Bimaristan
place.lede: Four levels, and the routes between them. Where you are, what is next door, and what has changed since you arrived.
tier.rawafid: Rawafid and the Outer Care Houses
place.nothing_changed_yet: Nothing has changed yet. Everything here is as you found it.
place.binding_hold: This plan is written, not drawn
place.binding_hold_body: The plan exists as a generated candidate and the rest of the design package does not — no state frames for the Gate or the ICU interruption, no character treatments, no instrument states, no transitions. Nothing here is bound: an inclusion reviewer has seen none of it, so every asset renders provisionally and the text equivalent stands on its own.
art.ordinary_shift.alt: An ordinary morning shift in the emergency and urgent-care courts: treatment curtains opening and closing faster than the clerk can update the board, observation cots holding people who are waiting for inpatient beds, and one rapid-consultation position turned into a family-information desk.
art.keyed_transfer_token.alt: A worn keyed transfer token on a ring, its mechanical notch and institutional emblem still legible, its administrative band abraded — the older token Ayyash carries, which does not appear on the duty register.
art.sealed_arch.alt: A sealed arch in the Underworks closing an old transfer chamber. Its threshold bears an unfamiliar emblem. The mapped conduits stop before it; later ones continue through the wall.
art.quality_house.alt: Dar al-Itqan, the House of Quality and Patient Safety: reading desks, source-marked chronologies and hanging records, where evidence is administered and its meaning is argued over.
art.bimaristan_cutaway.alt: The Bimaristan cut open along one face, so that four levels are visible at once. At the top the Crown: wide floors with very few people on them, a signal tower, and the shelf carrying the Hall of Measure. Below it the Houses, the care rings — long wards of two rows of cots opening onto planted courts, teaching halls, laboratories, kitchens. Below those the Commons, the busiest level in the picture: the main gate, the arrival and sorting courts, storehouses and transport yards, shaded by awnings and crowded. Beneath all of it the Underworks, older than everything above and built in six centuries of layers by people who did not consult each other, so the brickwork changes character every few paces: cisterns, conduits, pressure chambers and waste channels, lamps on hooks at the junctions and darkness between them, chalk marks on almost every surface, and one sealed arch closing a forgotten junction where two conduits that the official map shows as separate pass through the same chamber. A line of towers, lanterns, bells and message rails runs the full height of the building like a spine, and a single taut wire climbs from a water-driven clock in the Underworks to the bell frame at the summit: the hour begins at the bottom and is answered downward. Beyond the walls the city of Rawafid recedes into farms, wells and waterways.

place.plan_provisional: A generated candidate, shown while it waits for inclusion review. It is not canon: incidental architectural, costume, equipment and emblem details do not become part of the world by appearing in an image.
response.01.02.stabilize.environment: Nothing arrives. The bay stays as it is — lamp light, hands on bags, a nurse counting aloud so somebody else can keep the rhythm. Beyond the doorway the ward is lit, and the difference across that doorway is the whole picture.
response.01.02.stabilize.instrument: The staffing board does not change. It counts positions, and what changed is who is standing where.
response.01.02.stabilize.holder: The hands holding the bay are in the bay, and they came from somewhere the duty nursing leader can name.
response.01.02.bridge.environment: The set comes up the service passage on its frame, through a door that takes it. Equipment in the bay comes back on — not the room lights, the equipment — and the hands come off one at a time.
response.01.02.bridge.instrument: The critical-power board does not change. It watches the generator and the main critical bus, and the bay is now supplied by neither.
response.01.02.bridge.holder: The mobile reserve is in intensive care. Emergency care does not have it.
response.01.02.relocate.environment: Beds go out through the doorway one at a time, each with somebody walking beside it. The bay empties around the work at the board.
response.01.02.relocate.instrument: The staffing board changes, and gets worse at describing the ward: the far bay reads emptier, the receiving positions read fuller, and neither number says that the same people are covering both.
response.01.02.relocate.holder: The people walking beside the beds are the people who were covering somewhere else.
